shortsmith-vs-opusclip.title: Shortsmith vs OpusClip: A Sourced Comparison
shortsmith-vs-opusclip.description: Shortsmith vs OpusClip compared on deployment, pricing model, watermarks, model choice, and workflow, with a source linked for every claim.
shortsmith-vs-opusclip.summary: A side-by-side of what each product documents, where the two differ, and which one fits your workflow.
shortsmith-vs-opusclip.notCovered: Not covered by the sources below

0.question: Is Shortsmith better than OpusClip?
0.answer: It depends on what you need. Shortsmith is the stronger fit if you want source access, self-hosting, or your own choice of AI models. OpusClip is the stronger fit if you want a managed product with a free tier to try. We don't claim either produces better clips, because we haven't run a controlled test that would support that.

1.question: Does Shortsmith add a watermark?
1.answer: No. Shortsmith's rendering pipeline has no watermark step, in the hosted app or a self-hosted install. OpusClip's help center says free-plan exports can include an OpusClip watermark.

2.question: Does hosted Shortsmith have a free plan?
2.answer: No. The hosted app requires a Pro or Creator subscription to process videos. The free route is self-hosting the open-source code, where there are no plan limits; you pay only for your own infrastructure and any AI providers you configure.

3.question: Which one is faster or makes better clips?
3.answer: We haven't published a controlled test of speed or clip quality, so we don't make that claim. Results depend on your videos and settings; the fair-test steps on this page show how to compare them on your own content.

shortsmith-vs-opusclip.intro: OpusClip helped define AI clipping: upload a long video, get short vertical clips back. Shortsmith does the same job as an open-source project you can use hosted or run yourself. This comparison sticks to what each product documents. Shortsmith claims link to our source code. OpusClip claims link to OpusClip's own help center. Where a source doesn't cover something, the table says so rather than guessing.
shortsmith-vs-opusclip.introNote: This page doesn't rate clip quality, caption accuracy, or processing speed. To compare those, see <test>how to run your own test</test>.

verdict.heading: The short answer
verdict.shortsmith: Choose Shortsmith if you want to self-host, inspect or modify the code, pick your own AI models (including fully local ones), or export without a watermark.
verdict.opusclip: Choose OpusClip if you want a managed product you never have to deploy, and want to start on a free plan.

pricing.heading: Pricing model: credits vs. plans vs. your own infrastructure
pricing.p1: OpusClip's <plans>plans and credits article</plans> describes paid plans that use credits for processing minutes, plus a free plan. Its <watermark>watermark article</watermark> says free-plan exports can carry an OpusClip watermark. Plan prices and credit amounts change, so check OpusClip's current pricing page instead of relying on numbers copied into a blog post.
pricing.p2: Shortsmith offers two routes. The hosted app has <pro>{proName}</pro> at ${proPrice}/month for {proLimit} hours of video in 720p and <scale>{scaleName}</scale> at ${scalePrice}/month for {scaleLimit} hours in 1080p, with yearly billing at two months free. There is no free hosted plan; processing requires a subscription. The self-hosted route is free software with no plan limits. You pay for the server and any AI APIs you configure, and the <guide>self-hosting guide</guide> shows a fully local setup with no per-request AI fees.

chooseShortsmith.heading: When Shortsmith is the better fit
chooseShortsmith.li1: You need control over where video goes. Self-hosting keeps the app, database, and rendered clips on your infrastructure. With Whisper and Ollama, transcription and clip selection run locally too.
chooseShortsmith.li2: You have a large back catalog. Self-hosted installs have no monthly video cap. Throughput depends on your hardware and provider limits.
chooseShortsmith.li3: You want to change how clips are chosen. The selection prompt, scoring, caption templates, and rendering are all in the repository.
chooseShortsmith.li4: You're building clipping into another tool. API keys, a REST API, and an MCP server let scripts and AI agents create and download clips.

chooseOpusclip.heading: When OpusClip is the better fit
chooseOpusclip.li1: You don't want to operate anything. Self-hosting means managing Docker, provider keys, updates, and backups.
chooseOpusclip.li2: You want to try before paying. OpusClip documents a free plan (with a possible watermark). Hosted Shortsmith has no free tier.
chooseOpusclip.li3: You rely on features not covered here. If a specific OpusClip workflow matters to you, confirm it on opus.pro and test whether Shortsmith covers it before switching.

test.heading: How to run your own fair test
test.intro: The comparison that matters most is one on your own content:
test.li1: Pick two or three recordings that represent your channel: one easy (single speaker), one hard (multiple speakers, screen shares).
test.li2: Run each through both tools with default settings, and note the time from submission to finished clips.
test.li3: Shuffle the clips and review them without knowing which tool made each. Score whether each clip makes sense without context, has a clear hook, frames the speaker correctly, and has accurate captions.
test.li4: Count the edits each clip needs before you'd post it. Editing time is a cost the subscription price doesn't show.
test.demo: Want to see Shortsmith output first? The <demo>demo page</demo> shows real clips next to links to the original timestamps.

self-host-shortsmith-docker.title: How to Self-Host Shortsmith with Docker Compose
self-host-shortsmith-docker.description: Self-host Shortsmith, the open-source AI video clipper: requirements, .env setup, a fully local Whisper + Ollama option, first-run checks, and a production checklist.
self-host-shortsmith-docker.summary: A practical walkthrough of the repository's Docker Compose stack: what each service does, which keys you need, how to run without cloud AI, and what to harden before production.

0.question: Is self-hosted Shortsmith free?
0.answer: The code is free under AGPL-3.0 and self-host mode has no generation limits or paywall. You still pay for your own hardware or server, and for any cloud transcription or LLM usage you configure. A Whisper + Ollama setup avoids per-request AI fees but needs enough local compute.

1.question: Can Shortsmith run without any cloud AI services?
1.answer: Yes, for clip analysis. Set TRANSCRIPTION_PROVIDER=whisper to transcribe locally and LLM=ollama:<model> to select clips with a local model. Downloading YouTube links still needs internet access; uploaded files do not. Optional B-roll uses the Pexels API.

2.question: Do I need a GPU?
2.answer: No. The .env.example template sets BACKEND_CPU_ONLY=true, which installs CPU-only PyTorch. CPU-only Whisper transcription is slower than a cloud API, so long videos take longer on modest hardware.

3.question: Does it work on Apple Silicon?
3.answer: Yes, with a caveat: the backend and worker images run as linux/amd64 under emulation. BACKEND_CPU_ONLY=true avoids NVIDIA downloads, but it does not enable Apple GPU acceleration.

4.question: How do I keep my instance private?
4.answer: Create your account, then set DISABLE_SIGN_UP=true and recreate the frontend container. Compose binds every port to 127.0.0.1, so nothing is public until you add a reverse proxy.

self-host-shortsmith-docker.intro: Shortsmith is an open-source AI video clipper based on SupoClip. The same repository ships a Docker Compose stack you can run on a laptop, a home server, or a VPS. This guide follows that stack exactly as it exists in the <repo>repository</repo>. Where a step depends on your provider or hardware, we say so instead of guessing.
self-host-shortsmith-docker.introChoice: Prefer not to run infrastructure? The <hosted>hosted app</hosted> runs the same pipeline. Still deciding between tools? Read our <comparison>Shortsmith vs OpusClip comparison</comparison> first.

stack.heading: What you are running
stack.lead: docker compose up starts these containers, all defined in docker-compose.yml:
stack.caption: Services in the Shortsmith Docker Compose stack

frontend.role: Next.js web app, auth, and API proxy

worker.role: ARQ worker: download, transcribe, analyze, render

redis.role: Redis 7: job queue and live progress

mcp.role: MCP server for AI clients (optional to keep running)

stack.after: Every published port is bound to 127.0.0.1, so a fresh install is reachable only from the machine itself. Generated clips, uploads, Postgres, and Redis are stored in named Docker volumes, so they survive container restarts. If you don't use MCP, stop that container with docker compose stop mcp.

requirements.heading: Requirements
requirements.li1: Docker with Compose v2 (docker compose) or the standalone docker-compose, plus Git.
requirements.li2: A transcription source, set with TRANSCRIPTION_PROVIDER: assemblyai (default, needs ASSEMBLY_AI_API_KEY), whisper (local, no key), or youtube_captions (YouTube links only).
requirements.li3: An LLM for clip selection, set with LLM=provider:model: OpenAI, Google, Anthropic, OpenRouter (each needs its API key), or a local ollama: model.
requirements.note: The first image build downloads Python and Node dependencies. The <quickstart>quick start</quickstart> estimates 5–10 minutes; it varies with your connection and CPU.

install.heading: Install with Docker Compose
install.clone: 1. Clone and create your environment file
install.providersBody: The template defaults to LLM=openrouter:anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5. Processing fails unless you set OPENROUTER_API_KEY or point LLM at a provider you have a key for. A minimal cloud setup looks like this:
install.secrets: Generate each secret with openssl rand -base64 32. SELF_HOST=true (the default) keeps billing off and removes per-account generation limits.
install.open: Open http://localhost:3107, create an account, and paste a YouTube, Twitch, or Kick link or upload a file. API docs are at http://localhost:8000/docs.

local.heading: Option: fully local transcription and clip selection
local.intro: To keep transcripts and analysis on your own hardware, combine local Whisper with an Ollama model:
local.worker: The worker makes the Ollama calls from inside its container, so Ollama must be reachable from there, not just from your shell. How you get there depends on where Ollama runs:
local.desktopHeading: Ollama on the host, with Docker Desktop (macOS, Windows)
local.desktop: No extra setup. Docker Desktop forwards host.docker.internal to the host, so leave OLLAMA_BASE_URL empty and pull the model with ollama pull gpt-oss:20b.
local.linuxHeading: Ollama on the host, with Docker Engine (Linux)
local.linux: Compose maps host.docker.internal to the Docker bridge gateway, but Ollama listens only on 127.0.0.1 by default, so the worker's connection is refused. Make Ollama listen on all interfaces:
local.expose: That also exposes port 11434 on your network interfaces. Ollama has no authentication, so block that port from outside the machine with your firewall. If your firewall filters traffic from Docker networks, also allow the containers to reach it.
local.container: Add it to the stack with an override file, then point Shortsmith at the service name instead of the host:
local.labelOverride: docker-compose.override.yml (merge into any override you already have)
local.whichever: Whichever setup you choose, test from inside the worker before submitting a video. The check looks for gpt-oss:20b because that is the model in the example LLM value. If you chose another model, replace it with the exact name after ollama: in your LLM setting. Ollama lists a model pulled without a tag as name:latest, so use that form in the check.
local.ready: model ready means the worker can reach Ollama and the model you searched for is installed. No output means either the connection failed or the model is missing, so rerun the command without the grep to see which. Smaller Whisper models trade accuracy for speed, and clip quality depends on the LLM. Compare a local model against a hosted one on a recording you know before switching your whole backlog.

verify.heading: Verify the install
verify.li1: Create an account and submit a short video first, so a misconfiguration fails fast.
verify.li2: Confirm the task page shows progress updates. If it stays queued, check the worker logs.
verify.li3: Play and download a finished clip.
verify.stuck: Stuck tasks are usually a missing provider key or a worker that cannot reach Redis. The <guide>troubleshooting guide</guide> covers the common cases.

production.heading: Production checklist
production.intro: The Compose file is tuned for getting started. Before putting it on a public domain:
production.li1: Build the production frontend. Compose defaults to the hot-reloading development target and mounts frontend/src into the container. Set FRONTEND_BUILD_TARGET=runner and NODE_ENV=production in .env, then drop the source mounts with the override below.
production.li2: Terminate HTTPS at a reverse proxy (Caddy, nginx, Traefik) in front of the frontend port.
production.li3: Expose the backend for uploads. With BACKEND_AUTH_SECRET set, browsers upload video files directly to NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL. Point that at a public HTTPS backend URL, and add your frontend origin to CORS_ORIGINS.
production.li4: Set your public origin everywhere: NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL, BETTER_AUTH_URL, and CORS_ORIGINS. NEXT_PUBLIC_* values are baked in at build time, so rebuild the frontend after changing them.
production.li5: Change the database password. docker-compose.yml hardcodes supoclip_password in four places: POSTGRES_PASSWORD in the postgres service and DATABASE_URL in the frontend, backend, and worker services. Editing POSTGRES_PASSWORD in .env alone changes none of them. Override all four, as shown below.
production.li6: Set REDIS_PASSWORD; the Redis container enables AUTH when it is non-empty.
production.li7: Close sign-ups with DISABLE_SIGN_UP=true if the instance is just for your team.
production.li8: Review the limits: MAX_VIDEO_DURATION (default 5400 s, 90 minutes) and MAX_VIDEO_UPLOAD_BYTES (default 4 GB).
production.passwordIntro: For the database password, put a new value in POSTGRES_PASSWORD in .env. Generate it with openssl rand -hex 24, because hex needs no escaping inside a URL. Then point all four settings at it in the same override file:
production.labelPassword: docker-compose.override.yml (merge into any override you already have)
production.existing: Postgres reads POSTGRES_PASSWORD only when it initializes an empty data volume. On an install that already has a database, changing that variable does not change the actual password. Rotate it inside Postgres first, using the same value as in .env. Then recreate the services so they use the new URLs:
production.docs: <config>docs/configuration.md</config> lists every variable, and <setup>docs/setup.md</setup> covers custom ports and public URLs.

upgrade.heading: Upgrades and backups
upgrade.intro: init.sql creates the schema only when the Postgres volume is first initialized. After that, nothing updates the schema automatically. If a new version adds files under frontend/prisma/migrations or backend/migrations, apply them yourself before you restart the app. New code running against the old schema fails on missing columns and tables. Back up first, and stop the app services so they don't pick up new code early. The development frontend hot-reloads mounted source.
upgrade.apply: Read each listed file, then apply it in a single transaction. Apply Prisma migrations in timestamp order and backend migrations in number order:
upgrade.prisma: A database created by init.sql has no Prisma migration history. Don't run prisma migrate deploy against it: Prisma would replay every migration from the first one and fail on tables that already exist. If you want Prisma to manage migrations from now on, first baseline it with
upgrade.prismaAfter: , but only for migrations whose changes are already in your schema. Prisma permanently skips any migration you mark as applied, even if its changes are missing.
upgrade.volumes: Back up the clips and uploads volumes too if you need to keep rendered videos. Never run docker compose down -v on an instance you care about: it deletes every volume, including the database.
upgrade.customize: Want to customize the output? Drop .ttf fonts into backend/fonts/ and .mp4 transitions into backend/transitions/. They appear in the app automatically. For automation, create an API key in Settings and use the REST API or the bundled MCP server.

best-free-opusclip-alternative.title: Free OpusClip Alternative: Self-Hosting Costs and Tradeoffs
best-free-opusclip-alternative.description: Looking for a free OpusClip alternative? Understand what self-hosting Shortsmith costs, what you maintain, and when a paid hosted workflow is a better fit.
best-free-opusclip-alternative.summary: The Shortsmith source is free. This guide explains the hardware, provider costs, and maintenance behind a self-hosted clipping workflow so you can decide whether it fits.
best-free-opusclip-alternative.lead: A free OpusClip alternative can remove a subscription fee without removing the work of running the tool. Shortsmith gives you an open-source clipping application you can self-host. The practical question is whether operating it is a better use of your time than using a paid hosted service.

audience.0: Creators clipping YouTube videos into shorts

best-free-opusclip-alternative.p1: Separate three decisions before choosing a free clipping workflow: which editing capabilities you need, who runs the processing, and which services your configuration calls. A free source-code license answers only part of that question.
best-free-opusclip-alternative.p2: Shortsmith is a self-hosted option for creators and technical teams who want the application source, editable captions and framing, and control over their processing setup. Your costs can include hardware, storage, maintenance, and external transcription or AI usage. You can also <hosted>use hosted Shortsmith</hosted> on a paid plan if you prefer managed processing.

verdict.heading: Quick Verdict
verdict.body: Self-host Shortsmith when control and customization justify maintaining the stack. Choose managed hosting when your priority is producing clips without operating infrastructure. Compare complete monthly costs, including your review and maintenance time.

why.heading: What “Free” Leaves for You to Pay
why.p1: Estimate the source-video hours you expect to process each month. Add storage for originals and exports, compute time, backups, and any paid transcription or model calls. If you already own suitable hardware, those costs differ from renting a server just for clipping.
why.p2: Include setup and recurring maintenance in that estimate. A local model can reduce external API usage while increasing demands on your machine. OpusClip documents its own plan, credit, and watermark rules; use those current sources when comparing the hosted option instead of assuming every free plan has the same limits.

different.heading: What Makes Shortsmith Different
different.p1: Shortsmith is not just a thin wrapper around a hosted editor. It is a complete open-source clipping app with a FastAPI backend, a Next.js frontend, background workers, transcription, AI scoring, face-aware vertical reframing, caption styling, and export presets.
different.p2: That makes the tradeoff clear. You take on setup, but you gain ownership. You can inspect the code, adapt it to your workflow, and decide which hosted AI providers or local models to use. The <guide>self-hosting guide</guide> walks through the setup, including a fully local Whisper + Ollama option.

compare.heading: Shortsmith vs OpusClip
compare.body: The summary below covers the essentials. For a row-by-row comparison with a source for every claim, read <comparison>Shortsmith vs OpusClip: a sourced comparison</comparison>.

0.shortsmith: Open source and self-hostable with no plan limits. Your costs are your own compute and API keys. The hosted app is paid.
0.opusclip: Free plan exists, but exports can include an OpusClip watermark.

1.shortsmith: Transcribes long videos, scores segments, and surfaces promising short-form moments.
1.opusclip: AI clipping workflow built for finding social-ready clips from long videos.

2.shortsmith: Face-centered 9:16 cropping, subtitles, and platform-ready exports.
2.opusclip: Offers short-form exports and AI reframing for social platforms.

3.shortsmith: Full source access, editable deployment, and no vendor lock-in.
3.opusclip: Hosted product with managed workflows and subscription tiers.

steps.0: Paste a YouTube, Twitch, or Kick URL or upload a video.
steps.1: Shortsmith transcribes the source and finds candidate moments.
steps.2: AI scores clips for hook strength, engagement, value, and shareability.
steps.3: The editor creates vertical, captioned clips with face-aware framing.
steps.4: You export shorts for YouTube Shorts, TikTok, Instagram Reels, or other feeds.

better.heading: When Shortsmith Is the Better Choice
better.body: Self-hosted Shortsmith fits a team that can operate Docker services and wants to change the pipeline, select its providers, or integrate clipping with its own systems. Start with one familiar recording, verify the output, and measure the effort before committing a backlog.

opus.heading: When OpusClip May Still Be Better
opus.body: OpusClip may still be the better fit if you want the convenience of a polished hosted service and do not want to think about deployment, infrastructure, model keys, queues, or maintenance.

cta.kicker: Free if you self-host, paid plans if you don't

0.question: Is a self-hosted OpusClip alternative really free?
0.answer: The Shortsmith source has no license fee under AGPL-3.0. You still provide compute, storage, maintenance, and any paid transcription or AI usage. Compare those costs with a hosted plan before deciding.

1.question: Is Shortsmith completely free?
1.answer: The Shortsmith codebase is free and open source, and self-hosted installs have no plan limits. You still pay for your own infrastructure and any transcription or LLM provider you configure. The hosted app requires a paid plan.

2.question: Does Shortsmith add a watermark?
2.answer: No. Shortsmith's rendering pipeline has no watermark step, whether you use the hosted app or a self-hosted install.
